headline: A quieter weekend than feared: Trump says there is no rush to strike Iran before Tuesday's vote, OPEC+ held output, and China's factories shrank; the risk days are still Wednesday and Thursday, when five 'Buy zone now' names report.
summary: Markets last traded Friday Oct 30, and the dashboard is current on those closes (prices_as_of 2026-10-30). Over the weekend Trump said the US is in no hurry to strike Iran again, Rubio said no decision has been made, and Fox reported new strikes are unlikely before the Nov 3 vote; a separate report still says the US warned Gulf allies of strikes as early as Nov 4. Iran's foreign minister floated a two day Hormuz reopening if the US meets Tehran's terms, but said Iran will not meet US officials now, which undercuts Saturday's report of direct talks. OPEC+ kept December output unchanged on Nov 1, and China's official factory index fell to 49.3, a contraction. This week, NICE, PODD and RELY report Wednesday and AFRM and ZTS Thursday, so half of the 'Buy zone now' list has a report inside the next five days. US futures open Sunday 6pm ET (3pm Pacific); no futures or Asia prices are in yet.

regime.why: Nothing traded over the weekend, so Friday's risk off close stands: the S&P 500 is down three weeks in a row and QQQ is only 1.6% above its 200 day average. The weekend news leaned slightly calmer (no strike before the vote, OPEC+ steady), but the Iran decision, the vote count and two central bank decisions all land Tuesday to Thursday.

signals.title: Iran: Trump says no rush to strike before the vote; Iran floats a two day Hormuz reopening but rules out meeting the US for now
signals.since_yesterday: Trump said Oct 31 the US is 'not in that much of a hurry' to strike, and Iran's foreign minister said Iran has no plan to meet US officials now, which undercuts Saturday's report of direct US talks in Doha.
signals.what_happened: On Oct 31 Rubio said Trump has not decided whether to resume strikes and prefers a diplomatic end; Trump said the US is 'not in that much of a hurry' and that 'one or two sites' remain (Fox, CBS). Trump has said there will be no new attacks before the Nov 3 vote but has not ruled them out after (Jerusalem Post citing Reuters, Nov 1). Iranian negotiators held a third day of talks with Qatari mediators in Doha on Nov 1. Foreign Minister Araghchi said a plan with Qatar could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days, but only if the US first lifts sanctions, restores oil waivers, frees Iranian funds and cuts its forces in the region; the US rejected an earlier one week version (AP via Fox, The Tribune). Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered an 'unrestricted response' to any attack. CENTCOM said it has redirected 144 ships under its blockade, and Saudi air defenses downed a drone near Riyadh on Oct 31 (Fox).
signals.so_what: The strike risk did not go away; it moved to after the vote, which is exactly the Nov 4 window from Saturday's report. The Iranian offer is real movement but its terms ask the US to give first, so a quick deal is unlikely. Who pays if talks fail: airlines and fuel heavy businesses. Who gets paid if Hormuz reopens: tanker owners and Gulf exporters, while oil producers lose some of the war premium. What would make this wrong: a US reply to the two day plan before Wednesday.
signals.for_you: Swing: no new oil or airline trades before Wednesday. XOM and CVX are past their 2R targets on a close; the plan is still to take it or sell half and move the stop to the entry. DAL is now 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' (lower highs and lower lows), so no DAL buy or put either way.

signals.title: OPEC+ kept December output unchanged; Gulf members still pump below their targets
signals.since_yesterday: The Nov 1 meeting confirmed the hold that sources had flagged.
signals.what_happened: Seven OPEC+ members agreed on Nov 1 to keep December output targets unchanged, after unwinding the last of their voluntary cuts in September (Bloomberg). Reuters sources said further changes will wait until next year, and the group must finish a capacity review this quarter before setting 2027 baselines (CNBC, Oct 31). Bloomberg noted the Gulf members are still pumping well below their targets because of the war.
signals.so_what: A hold was expected, so it changes little for Monday. The bigger point is that higher targets do not add barrels while Gulf exports are constrained. Oil prices this week depend on Iran, not on OPEC+.
signals.for_you: No action. No puts on energy names into the Nov 4 window.

signals.title: China's factory index fell back into contraction at 49.3
signals.what_happened: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1, below the 50.0 Reuters poll; the non manufacturing index fell to 49.7 from 50.2 (NBS, Oct 31). Large firms held at 50.2, while medium firms fell to 48.4 and small firms to 47.5. High tech manufacturing stayed at 51.3. The statistics bureau blamed demand pulled forward before the National Day holiday and a complex world backdrop.
signals.so_what: Weak Chinese demand at a time of $113 oil is a squeeze for China's factories and a drag on metals demand. The high tech number shows Beijing's chip and equipment push is still spending. Second order: a weak China makes Beijing more likely to add stimulus, which is the usual trigger for a bounce in Chinese stocks, but nothing has been announced.
signals.for_you: No action. Chinese ADRs are not on the buy zone list. BABA and PDD are marked hurt on the China page.

signals.title: Brazil: the market is shut Monday, and forecasts split before Wednesday's rate decision
signals.since_yesterday: Sao Paulo is closed Monday for All Souls' Day, and Polymarket's odds of a hold rose to 81.2% while the Focus survey still expects a cut.
signals.what_happened: Brazil's stock market is closed Monday Nov 2 (Rio Times, Nov 1). For the Copom decision on Wednesday Nov 4, the central bank's Focus survey median points to a 0.25 point cut to 13.50%, while Polymarket gives 81.2% to a hold at 13.75%. It is not known whether the government will publish a spending plan before the meeting. The decision comes in the evening Brasilia time; Brasilia is now 2 hours ahead of Eastern after the US clock change.
signals.so_what: With Sao Paulo shut, any Monday move shows up only in EWZ and the New York listed shares, then again on Tuesday at home. The split forecast matters: the Focus number partly reflects views from before the election shock, and markets now lean to a hold. A cut with the real weak would be a surprise that could hit the currency.
signals.for_you: No Brazil buys, swings or new puts before Wednesday evening. NU (11.61, Oct 30) stays Wait under its 13.10 line.

signals.title: This week: five 'Buy zone now' names report, and Apple opens the week Monday
signals.what_happened: Apple and Palantir report Monday after the close (CNBC); Apple consensus is $1.99 a share on $113.4 billion of revenue (CMC Markets). AAPL closed at 344.63 on Oct 30 (Massive) and is rated Wait. AMD reports Tuesday. Among the 'Buy zone now' names, NICE, PODD and RELY report Wednesday Nov 4, and AFRM and ZTS Thursday Nov 5 (dashboard earnings dates). APH, MSFT, PYPL, BLK and COF have no report this week. The list changed after Saturday's chart check, so this differs from Saturday's week ahead: LIVN and CF are no longer 'Buy zone now', and PODD, AFRM and ZTS are. In energy, NuScale reports Nov 5 after the close (secondary sources) and Oklo Nov 6 before the open (company).
signals.so_what: Half of the buy list carries a report risk inside five days, in the same week as the vote and a possible strike. That is a reason to wait, not a reason to sell. Apple matters for the whole tape because it spends far less on AI than the companies sold last week: a good report would say the selling is about AI spending, not about big tech in general.
signals.for_you: Long term: no buys or puts on NICE, PODD, RELY, AFRM or ZTS before their reports. If you add this week, the calm names are APH, MSFT and COF (PYPL and BLK closed just above their zone tops); a small first tranche at most, after Wednesday. Swing: none of these has a dashboard swing setup.

cycle.quadrant: Growth rising and inflation rising (overheating), with a soft spot in China
cycle.quadrant_why: US Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% pace (Oct 29) and Brent is $113.43 (Oct 30). China's factory index fell to 49.3 in October (NBS), a reminder that growth outside the US is weaker.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening, late. The RBA is expected to hike to 4.85% on Nov 3, and US futures price a December Fed hike (Barchart, Oct 30). The 10 year is 4.927%.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. Big AI spenders now fund the build partly with debt and new stock, and Brazil just repriced its debt path after the election.
cycle.big_cycle: Internal order: US midterms Tuesday. External order: the war on Iran, with strikes paused until after the vote and talks in Doha. Technology: the AI build has to show cash returns. Debt and money: central banks tightening into high oil.
tailwinds: OPEC+ is not cutting, and a Hormuz deal path exists (Araghchi, Nov 1).
Stocks have risen in the 12 months after every midterm since 1950 (24/7 Wall St).
headwinds: A possible US strike on Iran as early as Nov 4.
China's factory and service indexes both under 50 (NBS).
Rate hikes coming in Australia and priced in the US.

history.what: The S&P 500 has never had a losing 12 months after a midterm election since 1950 (24/7 Wall St, May 2026); LPL counts 18 of 18 positive since 1954, with an average gain of 18.2% (LPL via Webull).
history.lesson: The pattern is strong, but it is a small sample of 18 to 19 cases, and it measures a full year, not the next week. It says nothing about what an Iran strike on Nov 4 does to prices on Nov 5.

cycle.differences: Past post midterm rallies usually came with the Fed easing or about to ease. In 2026 futures price a Fed hike in December, oil is above $110 and the country is at war, so the base rate deserves less weight than usual.
cycle.for_you: Swing: stay small into Wednesday. Puts: none this week; the buy list names with reports are off limits and the rest are calm but not urgent. Long term: if you add, wait until after Wednesday and use the calm 'Buy zone now' names inside their zones (APH, MSFT, COF).
